accuracy.evidence: Checked against NGSS 4-ESS3-2 and its clarification (earthquake-resistant buildings, improved monitoring and warnings as example solutions), FEMA P-749 Earthquake-Resistant Design Concepts (braced frames, soft or weak storeys failing first, base isolation with elastomeric bearings, why added mass raises seismic forces), NOAA's National Tsunami Warning Center and DART buoy pages (seismometers detect the quake, deep-ocean pressure sensors confirm the wave, warning centres issue alerts), NZ Civil Defence 'Long or Strong, Get Gone' and Drop, Cover and Hold guidance. Deep-ocean tsunami speed: sqrt(g·d) at 4,000 m is about 713 km/h, so 'about 700 km in an hour' is right; every parameterised answer (2n, t − w, r·k, 700h) was checked at the corners of its ranges by gate_items. The pin-jointed frame is named as such, so 'the square leans like a hinge' is not a wrong claim about rigid-jointed steel frames.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented ideas from FEMA's public-education material and tsunami-safety campaigns: more sides or more mass makes a frame stronger (step 1 predict, tag heavy), bracing the top rather than the soft ground storey (step 2 predict, four position-specific shake-test messages, p4, tags top and flex), rigidly fixing a building to the ground is safest (step 3 predict, m6, tag bolt), waiting for an official siren after a long strong coastal quake (step 5 predict, m4, tag wait), going to look at the sea (tag look), rivers and low bridges as refuges (route message, m5, tag river), and running outside while shaking (tags run and stand).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). 583 What is an earthquake and 912 Measuring earthquake strength explain causes and magnitude; 961 Tsunamis covers how the wave forms; 969 Tectonic Plates is about boundaries. None has a frame to brace, a soft-storey shake test, base isolation with a vase that tips or stays, a warning-chain ordering task or an escape-route map. The mechanisms here (triangulation, storey shear, isolation, warning chain, evacuation by height) are specific to designing for earthquakes.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea comes from doing: the unbraced frame stays leaning at the angle reported in degrees and the braced one only shivers; the shake test cracks exactly the unbraced floors and the message changes when only the ground floor is left open; shaking with no bearings tips the vase, with some bearings is named as half-fixed, and with all three leaves the vase upright while the ground visibly slides; choosing a card too early says what must happen first; picking a low route names the height and why it floods.

predictions.evidence: Step 1: 'the square, it has more sides' is tempting, and pushing the frame disproves it. Step 2: 'the top floor' or 'all the same' is tempting, and the shake test shows the open ground floor folding first. Step 3: 'worse, because it can slide' is tempting, and the vase stays up only on bearings. Step 5: 'wait for the siren' is tempting, and the reveal and route feedback say a long, strong quake is itself the warning.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Eight challenge questions; every distractor has its own WHY entry in shake_art.js (heavy, glue, top, flex, bounce, bolt, skip, before, wait, look, river, low, stop, adults, run, stand), each naming the specific slip. In the lab, the shake test has four different messages depending on which floors were left open, partial bearings get their own message, each warning card has a 'what must come first' message, and both wrong routes have their own reason.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py gives the kid text grade 3.1 (limit 6.5) and the adult text 7.6 (limit 9.5). Kid sentences are short and concrete ('Add one diagonal beam and the square becomes two triangles.'); the precise terms for the band (cross-brace, seismometer, bearings, tsunami, evacuation, drill) are each explained in plain words where they first appear, and soft storey and base isolation are in the key idea and adult text.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases. The four kid paragraphs match the frame, tower, bearings and warning/route steps; the adult text gives the standard, what each task shows and the named mistakes; every hint points back to something the learner saw in the lab (the triangles, the vase, River Lane).

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (Android, 2x) for every step at start, mid Show me and end, in light and dark themes, plus desktop (gate_browser on iPhone 13 and 1200 px). After the first pass the map was clipped to its frame (the hill rings ran outside it), roads were drawn light in dark mode, labels on the ground strip were made light in dark mode, the rubber bearings got a light outline in dark mode, and the canvas was made taller so the finished warning chain is not covered by the feedback box. Every action also has a full-width button.

accessibility.evidence: gate_browser passed: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, all 5 tasks complete with Show me, no console errors. Everything works with buttons as well as the canvas (Push the top, Add a diagonal brace, Brace each floor, Run the shake test, Fit a rubber bearing, Next card buttons, Take each road), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with the lean angle, floors braced, bearings fitted, shake-test result, the chain so far, and the chosen road.
